page: Amazon Web Services m6idn.8xlarge is a general-purpose, network and EBS-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs based on the x86_64 architecture, utilizing an Intel Xeon 8375C processor with 16 physical cores, 2 threads per core, and a clock speed of 3.5 GHz. The CPU cache configuration includes 48 KB of L1d cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 54 MB of L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, it includes a bundled 1900 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume. It offers a high baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps.

Benchmark results position the m6idn.8xlarge consistently in the average performance tier across multiple workloads. In CPU testing, it achieves a stress-ng single-core score of 1891.59 and a multi-core score of 30911.76, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 35392.93. Memory performance is characterized by a read-only small-block cached bandwidth of 1658.45 GB/sec, dropping to 146.7 GB/sec for large-block uncached reads, and 67.89 GB/sec for large-block writes. For database and web operations, the instance handles 30.66 million Redis SET operations per second and achieves a static web serving throughput of 31.29 GB/sec. Large-scale LLM inference is a notable bottleneck, with the 70B model prompt processing speed falling into the weak category at 6.05 tokens/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the m6idn.8xlarge offers a balanced resource density, combining high-speed baseline networking, local NVMe storage, and dedicated compute resources without the added expense of a GPU. The inclusion of local NVMe SSD storage and 50 Gbps network bandwidth makes it highly suitable for data-intensive applications, database operations, and web serving. It is well-suited for workloads such as relational databases, caching layers, software compilation, and general-purpose enterprise applications that require a balance of compute, memory, and fast local storage.
